acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given valid JSON, PHP, and JS files with markers, build() replaces marker content and returns a successful OperationResult.
When PHP target file is missing, returns an OperationResult error with ERROR_PHP_ICON_FILE_NOT_FOUND.
When JS target file is missing, returns an OperationResult error with ERROR_JS_ICON_FILE_NOT_FOUND.
When markers are missing in a target file, returns an OperationResult error with ERROR_START_MARKER_NOT_FOUND.
No dependency on LocalFrameworkClone or t() function.

summary: Created IconBuilder orchestrator class at src/classes/Application/Composer/IconBuilder/IconBuilder.php.

IconBuilder reads icons from JSON via IconsReader, renders PHP/JS methods using PHPRenderer and JSRenderer, and replaces content between /* START METHODS */ and /* END METHODS */ markers in target files.
Error constants ERROR_PHP_ICON_FILE_NOT_FOUND (82301), ERROR_JS_ICON_FILE_NOT_FOUND (82302), ERROR_START_MARKER_NOT_FOUND (82303) ported from the original Migrator class.
No dependency on LocalFrameworkClone or t() function.
Created 10 unit tests covering all acceptance criteria in tests/AppFrameworkTests/Composer/IconBuilder/IconBuilderTest.php.
All 10 tests pass. Pre-existing PHPStan error in FetchMany.php (unrelated) is the only analysis finding.

comments.note: IconBuilder.insertIconCode() passes the shared OperationResult instance for error reporting. This is correct and consistent with AppUtils patterns, but callers should note that any makeError() call on the returned result modifies the same object. The design is intentional and appropriate for this use case.

file_put_contents() is used directly for writing rather than AppUtils FileInfo::factory()->putContents(). Both are functionally equivalent here; the native call is simpler and avoids a dependency for a build-time class that must operate outside the full app bootstrap.

comments.note: insertIconCode() does not check the return value of file_put_contents(). A silent write failure (e.g. read-only file) would cause build() to return a valid OperationResult while the target file is unchanged. Low risk for a build-time tool operating on tracked source files, but could be hardened in a follow-up.

No validation that MARKER_END position is strictly after MARKER_START in insertIconCode(). If the end marker appears before the start marker in the file, substr() arithmetic produces malformed content. Requires deliberately corrupted target files and is outside any AC scope.

ERROR_START_MARKER_NOT_FOUND (82303) is reused for a missing end marker. The error message string correctly identifies which marker is absent, but the constant name is slightly misleading. Acceptable as-is since the tests explicitly assert this behavior.

summary: FAIL — one blocking issue: file_put_contents() return value is discarded in insertIconCode(). A write failure (permissions, disk full) silently returns a successful OperationResult while the target file is unchanged. This is a logic defect: build() can report success for an operation that did not occur.

All other dimensions PASS: clean architecture, correct OperationResult usage, typed constants, proper error constants, no t()/LocalFrameworkClone dependencies, well-structured tests with temp-file teardown.

comments.note: BLOCKING — insertIconCode() at line 189 discards the return value of file_put_contents(). The function returns false on failure (read-only file, full disk, etc.), but this is never checked. As a result, build() proceeds to return OperationResult::makeSuccess() even when neither target file was written. Fix: add ERROR_WRITE_FAILED = 82304, check the return value, and call $result->makeError() if it is false. A corresponding unit test (e.g. test_build_writeFailure_returnsError) using a chmod(0444) temp file should be added.

ERROR_START_MARKER_NOT_FOUND (82303) is reused for a missing end marker. The error message correctly names the absent marker, so this is not a runtime problem, but the constant name is misleading. Consider renaming to ERROR_MARKER_NOT_FOUND in a follow-up — this is a public API change and requires a test update, so out of scope for the current fix.

No validation that MARKER_END position is strictly after MARKER_START. If a file is manually corrupted with reversed marker order, the substr() arithmetic in insertIconCode() produces malformed output without any error signal. A guard (if $endPos <= $afterStart) should be added in a follow-up; outside current AC scope.

[documentation-forward] The build() docblock lists three error cases (missing PHP file, missing JS file, missing marker) but will need a fourth entry once ERROR_WRITE_FAILED is added. Update the @return and error-list prose in the docblock to cover write failure after the developer fix is applied.

comments.note: Used @ error suppression on file_put_contents() to prevent a spurious PHP warning from appearing in build output when a write fails. This is appropriate here: the return value is the authoritative signal, and the native warning adds no value for build-time tooling. A comment could be added to the source line to explain the intent, but it is not strictly necessary for such a well-understood pattern.
